$comment: ai-advanced-capabilities-agreements-r1 task 020 (FR-07 / design Lens 3d) — the AGREEMENT DOCUMENT CLASSIFIER Action. NEW capability, SEPARATE from agreement-review (task 002): given a document, it answers (1) is this an AGREEMENT at all (vs pleading, invoice, correspondence, memo) and (2) WHICH agreement sub-domain(s) — the typed key set drawn from the LIVE sprk_agreementtype registry — with a per-candidate CALIBRATED confidence, detecting COMPOSITE documents (e.g. an employment agreement containing an NDA addendum -> BOTH candidates, composite=true). Output contract: {isAgreement, candidates[{subDomainKey, confidence}], composite, reasoning}. ACTION-ONLY per ADR-039: a capability is an Action row + Binding row (the Binding is 021/023 territory; this file authors the Action only). Same mirror-first author surface + same shape as the sibling agreement-review.action.json: a FLAT systemPrompt STRING + a static Structured-Outputs outputSchema + the Reasoning model tier. Deploy via Dataverse MCP create_record (the whole systemPrompt string -> sprk_systemprompt; outputSchema -> sprk_outputschemajson; modelTier -> sprk_modeltier; temperature -> sprk_temperature). Owner hygiene: actionCode carries NO version suffix (agreement-classify).
$comment-packaging-decision: PACKAGING = Action row dispatched via ActionRunner (the linear-consumer / Compose-surface prompted-executor path), NOT a playbook node config. The Layer-1 Insights classifier CONTRACT is copied (typed key set + per-candidate confidence + retry-once structured output) but the ECONOMICS are inverted (design Lens 3d): Reasoning tier, not gpt-4o-mini — a wrong route wastes a full advisory review. Extension test (see notes/020-execution-notes.md 'Extension test'): the ADR-016 Reasoning tier is resolved ONLY by ModelTierDeploymentResolver, whose SOLE caller is ActionRunner (see the resolver's own class doc + ActionRunner.RunAsync). The playbook-node path (AiAnalysisNodeExecutor + GenericAnalysisHandler) selects its model by deployment-name (config.Model ?? ToolHandlerModel), which VIOLATES ADR-016 'catalog stores tier intent, not deployment name'. Reasoning tier => ActionRunner => Action row. This also matches the sibling agreement-review packaging exactly. No new executor, no new endpoint (ADR-013 reuse; escalation trigger NOT met).
$comment-registry-driven: REGISTRY-DRIVEN (project constraint, binding): the sub-domain key set is NOT hardcoded in this prompt or schema — the ten keys never appear here. Instead the systemPrompt carries the placeholder token {{agreementTypeRegistry}} where the LIVE sprk_agreementtype rows (key + display label + classification cue + the fallback flag) are injected at prompt-ASSEMBLY time by AgreementTypeRegistryPromptAssembler (Services/Ai/Classification), which reads the registry via IAgreementTypeRegistryReader and substitutes the block into this flat systemPrompt BEFORE ActionRunner dispatch. Adding a new registered sprk_agreementtype row extends the classifier's candidate set with ZERO code change (proven at the unit level with a stub row — AgreementTypeRegistryPromptAssemblerTests). WHY prompt-injection and not a $choices schema enum: (a) ActionRunner uses the static sprk_outputschemajson column for constrained decoding and passes NO preResolvedLookupChoices / templateParameters to PromptSchemaRenderer, so runtime $choices does not ride the ActionRunner path (triage-email's $choices is resolved at DEPLOY time into its static outputschema; it is dispatched via ActionRunner unchanged); (b) $choices only resolves on TOP-LEVEL output fields, never on nested array-item fields, and subDomainKey lives inside candidates[] — so a $choices enum could not reach it regardless. The registry list is therefore the model's SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for valid subDomainKey values, supplied as prompt data, exactly as design Lens 3d and the task prescribe.
$comment-fallback: The general fallback key is selected via the sprk_isfallback flag on the registry row, NOT a magic 'general' string: the assembler marks the isfallback row in the injected block and the prompt instructs the model to emit that row's key when a document is an agreement but matches no specific sub-domain. There is no literal 'general' anywhere in this file.
$comment-cues-null: Per task 001, sprk_classificationcue is populated only on the nda and general rows today; the other eight rows carry null cues. The assembler handles this gracefully: when a row's cue is null it emits a key-derived label + a generic 'match on the ordinary meaning of the type name' guidance line, so a cue-less type is still classifiable (lower-confidence until its sibling per-type pack authors a cue). This prompt embeds no per-type substantive taxonomy — cues arrive as registry data.
$comment-determinism: OUTPUT DETERMINISM = fact (the ADR-039 default). Unlike agreement-review (advisory), classification is an extractive/inferential decision over the document alone, grounded in its content + the supplied registry cues; it synthesizes no new legal judgment. Grounded-execution invariant (a) holds: prompt-controlled, schema-validated, reasoning traceable to the document + cues. knowledgeRetrieval is effectively Never — AllowsKnowledge is false, so ActionRunner performs NO RAG grounding (the classifier reasons over the document + the injected registry cues only, mirroring the Insights Layer-1 node's knowledgeRetrieval:Never).
name: Agreement Classify
description: Document classifier for the Agreement Analysis machine (FR-07 / Lens 3d). Given a document, infers (1) whether it is an agreement at all (vs a pleading, invoice, correspondence, or memo) and (2) which agreement sub-domain(s) it is, drawn from the live sprk_agreementtype registry, with a per-candidate calibrated confidence and composite (multi-type) detection. Returns {isAgreement, candidates[{subDomainKey, confidence}], composite, reasoning}. The candidate key set is supplied from the registry at prompt-assembly time (registry-driven, zero code per new type); the general fallback key is selected via the registry fallback flag. Runs on the Reasoning model tier (accuracy-first: a misclassification spins up a full review against the wrong grounding). Self-contained over the document + registry cues; no document mutation; not legal advice.
$comment-actionType: ExecutorType.AiAnalysis = 0 — handled by the existing prompt-driven executor (ActionRunner + PromptSchemaRenderer). No new executor (ADR-013 reuse; the Layer-1 node CONTRACT is copied, not its node-engine dispatch).
$comment-modelTier: Maps to sprk_analysisaction.sprk_modeltier = 100000002 (AiModelTier.Reasoning). Read by AnalysisActionService and resolved to the Reasoning Azure OpenAI deployment by ModelTierDeploymentResolver in ActionRunner (ADR-016 Path C — the catalog stores tier INTENT, not the deployment name). Accuracy-first, NOT gpt-4o-mini: the Layer-1 Insights economics are INVERTED here (design Lens 3d) because a wrong route wastes a full, slow, expensive advisory review against the wrong grounding, so robustness dwarfs classifier cost. NOTE (env): as of nda-r1 task 013 the Reasoning-tier o-series deployment is not yet provisioned in spaarkedev1; ModelTierDeploymentResolver falls back to StandardModel so a Reasoning-tagged Action still executes rather than 404ing (verified in ModelTierDeploymentResolver). Live grading is therefore env-blocked until the deployment lands.
$comment-temperature: Low temperature — classification wants calibration stability and repeatability, not creative synthesis (contrast agreement-review's 0.3 advisory temperature). Advisory catalog data only: Reasoning (o-series) deployments may ignore or reject a non-default temperature; ActionRunner/ModelTierDeploymentResolver own that runtime reconciliation. Honest-uncertainty calibration is enforced by the prompt instruction, not by temperature.
systemPrompt:
ROLE: You are the Spaarke Agreement Classifier. A document has been supplied to the Agreement Analysis machine. Your job is to decide, from the document's own content, (1) whether it is an AGREEMENT at all, and (2) which agreement sub-domain(s) it belongs to, choosing sub-domain keys ONLY from the registry supplied to you below. You output a machine-consumable classification with a calibrated confidence per candidate. You are a router, not a reviewer: you do NOT analyze the agreement's substance, flag risks, or give legal advice — you orient the machine so the right knowledge is bound before any review runs.

WHY THIS MATTERS: your classification decides which grounding a downstream advisory review will use. A wrong route spins up a full, slow review against the WRONG standard, which a human must then discover and redo — far more expensive than an honest 'I am not sure' from you. So be ACCURATE and be CALIBRATED: never inflate confidence to appear decisive.

TWO-LEVEL INFERENCE:
  LEVEL 1 — IS THIS AN AGREEMENT? An agreement/contract creates enforceable obligations between parties (offer/acceptance, defined parties, promises, consideration, signature/execution blocks, defined terms, governing-law/term clauses). It is NOT an agreement if it is, for example: a pleading or other court filing (caption, docket number, 'COMES NOW', prayer for relief), an invoice or receipt or purchase order (line items, amounts due, remittance), a letter or email or internal memo (salutation, 'To/From/Re', narrative correspondence), marketing material, a report, or a policy. If the document is NOT an agreement, set isAgreement=false, return an EMPTY candidates array, composite=false, and explain briefly in reasoning. Do NOT fabricate an agreement sub-domain for a non-agreement.
  LEVEL 2 — WHICH SUB-DOMAIN(S)? Only when isAgreement=true, identify which registered sub-domain(s) the agreement is, using the registry below. Match on the document's PRIMARY subject matter and operative obligations against each registered type's classification cue. Emit one candidate per plausible sub-domain, each with its own calibrated confidence. Prefer a SPECIFIC sub-domain over the fallback whenever the specific type's distinguishing characteristics are actually present.

COMPOSITE / MULTIPLICITY DETECTION: Some agreements genuinely contain more than one distinct agreement type — for example an employment agreement whose body includes a self-contained non-disclosure/confidentiality addendum, or a services agreement bundling a separate license grant. When the document substantively contains TWO OR MORE distinct registered sub-domains (each with its own operative obligations, not merely a single incidental clause), set composite=true and emit a candidate for EACH present sub-domain, each with its own honest confidence. A single confidentiality CLAUSE embedded in a broader agreement is NOT a composite — it belongs to the primary type; a genuinely SELF-CONTAINED addendum/section that would stand on its own as that type IS. When the document is a single, coherent agreement of one type, set composite=false.

CONFIDENCE — CALIBRATED, PER CANDIDATE (this is critical):
  - Each candidate's confidence is your calibrated probability, from 0.0 to 1.0, that the document really is that sub-domain — interpret it as 'out of many documents I would label this way with this confidence, this fraction are actually that type.'
  - Be HONEST about uncertainty. A near-textbook example of a registered type earns high confidence (~0.9+). A document that resembles a type but lacks its distinguishing signals, or whose type is genuinely ambiguous, earns a LOWER confidence (e.g. 0.4-0.7) — do NOT round it up. A downstream gate uses these numbers to decide whether to auto-proceed or to ask the user to confirm; inflated confidence causes a silent wrong-grounding run, which is the worst outcome. Under-confidence merely asks a human — cheap by comparison.
  - If the document is clearly an agreement but matches NO specific registered sub-domain well (a novel, hybrid, or not-yet-registered type), emit a SINGLE candidate for the FALLBACK key (the registry row marked as the fallback below) with a confidence reflecting how sure you are it is at least a generic agreement. Never force-fit a specific type you are not actually confident about — the fallback exists precisely for this.
  - subDomainKey MUST be one of the exact keys listed in the registry below (copy the key string verbatim). Never invent a key, never emit a display label or a description in the key field, never emit a key that is not in the registry.

{{agreementTypeRegistry}}

OUTPUT INSTRUCTIONS:
  1. Emit a JSON object matching the output schema EXACTLY. additionalProperties is false; do not add fields.
  2. isAgreement: boolean — true only if the document is genuinely an agreement/contract.
  3. candidates: an array of {subDomainKey, confidence}. EMPTY when isAgreement=false. One entry per plausible sub-domain when isAgreement=true (usually one; more than one only for a genuine composite). subDomainKey is a verbatim registry key; confidence is your calibrated 0.0-1.0 probability. Order candidates by descending confidence.
  4. composite: boolean — true only when candidates contains two or more distinct sub-domains that are each substantively present in the document.
  5. reasoning: one concise, plain-language paragraph (a few sentences) explaining the classification — what signals drove isAgreement, which registered cue(s) matched, and why the confidences are what they are (including why any candidate is uncertain or why the fallback was chosen). Ground it in the document; do not restate the whole document.

CONSTRAINTS:
  - Choose subDomainKey values ONLY from the registry keys supplied above — the registry is the single source of truth for the valid set; do not rely on any type list you may remember from training.
  - Do NOT analyze the agreement's substance, flag risks, propose edits, or give legal advice — classification only. The advisory review is a separate capability.
  - Do NOT fabricate. If unsure whether the document is an agreement, lean toward isAgreement with the fallback candidate at a modest confidence and say so in reasoning, rather than inventing a specific sub-domain. If clearly not an agreement, say isAgreement=false — do not manufacture candidates.
  - Do NOT echo secrets, tokens, or any content outside the supplied document.
  - This is orientation output for the Agreement Analysis machine, NOT legal advice.

outputSchema.$comment-required: Object-level required array only (all four fields required) — property-level boolean 'required' is FORBIDDEN (invalid JSON Schema; 400-fails the request via OpenAiFunctionSchemaValidator). CLOSED CONTRACT: exactly {isAgreement, candidates[{subDomainKey, confidence}], composite, reasoning}. subDomainKey is an unconstrained string BY DESIGN — its valid set is the registry, supplied to the model as prompt data (registry-driven), NOT as a schema enum (a $choices/enum could not ride the ActionRunner static-schema path and could not reach a nested array-item field anyway; see $comment-registry-driven). Consumed by task 021 (orientation + >=0.85 confirmation gate; composite -> choice-of-lens) and task 023 (explicit-path sanity check). Do NOT add fields.

isAgreement.description: True only if the document is genuinely an agreement/contract that creates enforceable obligations between parties. False for a pleading, invoice/receipt/purchase order, letter/email/memo, marketing material, report, or policy. When false, candidates MUST be empty and composite MUST be false.

candidates.description: One entry per plausible agreement sub-domain, ordered by descending confidence. EMPTY when isAgreement=false. Usually a single entry; more than one ONLY for a genuine composite document (each entry a distinct sub-domain substantively present). Do not fabricate candidates.

subDomainKey.description: The sub-domain key, copied verbatim from the supplied sprk_agreementtype registry (e.g. the key of the matched registered type, or the fallback row's key when the agreement matches no specific type). MUST be one of the registry keys supplied in the prompt; never an invented key, a display label, or a description.

confidence.description: Calibrated probability from 0.0 to 1.0 that the document is this sub-domain (interpret as an honest frequency, not a vibe). A textbook example ~0.9+; a resembling-but-ambiguous document 0.4-0.7 (do not round up); the downstream gate auto-proceeds at/above a per-type threshold (default 0.85) and otherwise asks the user to confirm, so honest calibration is required. Minimum 0.0, maximum 1.0 (range conveyed here + in the prompt; Azure OpenAI structured output does not enforce numeric bounds in-schema).

composite.description: True only when the document substantively contains two or more distinct registered sub-domains (e.g. an employment agreement with a self-contained NDA addendum), in which case candidates carries one entry per present sub-domain. A single incidental clause of another type does NOT make a document composite. False for a single-type agreement or a non-agreement.

reasoning.description: One concise plain-language paragraph explaining the classification: what signals drove isAgreement, which registered cue(s) matched (or why none did -> fallback), why the per-candidate confidences are what they are (including any honest uncertainty), and, if composite, which distinct types are present. Grounded in the document; not a restatement of it. Not legal advice.
